title: Pregnant Delhi SWAT Commando Beaten to Death With Dumbbell by Defence Ministry Husband
excerpt: Kajal Chaudhary, 27, died five days after her husband attacked her with a dumbbell. The family alleges prolonged dowry harassment despite the couple's love marriage.
body:
• Kajal Chaudhary, a 27-year-old Delhi Police SWAT commando who was four months pregnant, died on January 27 after her husband allegedly bludgeoned her with a metal dumbbell.
  • Her husband Ankur Chaudhary, a clerk with the Ministry of Defence, was arrested and charged with murder. He has been remanded to judicial custody at Tihar Jail.
  • Kajal's brother, a Delhi Police constable, says he was on the phone when the attack happened — Ankur allegedly told him to record the call as evidence before saying he was killing her.
  • The family alleges sustained dowry harassment despite the couple's love marriage in 2023, with demands for a car, cash, and repeated physical abuse.

A 27-year-old Delhi Police SWAT commando, four months pregnant, died on January 27 after her husband — a clerk in the Ministry of Defence — allegedly assaulted her with a metal dumbbell at their home in Mohan Garden, west Delhi. Kajal Chaudhary battled severe head injuries for five days at a hospital in Ghaziabad before succumbing, according to PTI.

Her husband, Ankur Chaudhary, 28, who was posted at Delhi Cantonment, was arrested within hours of the assault on January 22. Initially booked for attempt to murder, the charges were upgraded to murder and dowry death after Kajal died. He has been suspended from the Defence Ministry and sent to judicial custody at Tihar Jail, ANI reported.

A Phone Call That Captured the Final Moments

Kajal's brother Nikhil, a constable posted at Parliament Street Police Station, told PTI that he was on a phone call with his sister when the violence escalated. Ankur had initially called Nikhil and told him to "make your sister understand," saying she was arguing with him.

"He told me to put the call on recording, said it could be used as police evidence. Then he said he was killing her. I heard her screams before the call was cut off."

— Nikhil, Kajal's brother

According to Nikhil, Kajal had taken the phone to explain her situation but Ankur grew enraged that she was confiding in her brother, snatched the phone back, and announced his intent. About five minutes after the line went dead, Ankur called again. "He said, 'She is dead. Come to the hospital,'" Nikhil recalled, according to the Times of India.

When Nikhil arrived around midnight, Ankur's family was already at the hospital. Kajal had been declared brain dead. "When I saw my sister — not even an enemy kills someone like this," he told reporters.

Allegations of Dowry Harassment

Kajal's family has alleged that she endured prolonged dowry harassment from the early days of her marriage, despite it being a love marriage. The couple, both originally from Ganaur in Haryana, married in 2023 and had a one-and-a-half-year-old son.

Her father, Rakesh, told reporters that the family had given a Royal Enfield Bullet motorcycle, gold jewellery, and cash at the wedding. "But they said their son would have got a car had he married someone else. Even after my daughter arranged a car, they continued to harass her," he said, according to News Flash.

Kajal's mother said the family spent nearly ₹20 lakh on the marriage and accused Ankur of stealing ₹5 lakh. "Kajal endured a lot of suffering. Justice is what I seek. He is a monster," she said.

Police have said the immediate trigger for the January 22 assault was an argument over financial matters, though the family insists the violence was part of a pattern of dowry-related cruelty.

A Commando Who Could Not Escape Domestic Violence

Kajal joined the Delhi Police in 2022 and was posted with the SWAT unit of the Special Cell — one of the force's most elite divisions, trained to handle armed threats and high-risk operations. The bitter irony that a woman equipped to confront armed criminals was allegedly killed in her own home has prompted renewed scrutiny of domestic violence protections for women in uniform.

According to her brother, Kajal rarely spoke about the abuse at home. "She normally wouldn't tell us much about what was happening. But that day she was sharing her ordeal," Nikhil said.

Dowry Violence in India: The Broader Crisis

India recorded over 6,500 dowry deaths in 2022, according to the National Crime Records Bureau — roughly 18 women killed every day over dowry disputes. Despite stringent laws including Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code (dowry death) and Section 498A (cruelty by husband or relatives), enforcement remains inconsistent, and convictions are low.

For the Indian diaspora, cases like Kajal's underscore the persistence of dowry culture even in families with government employment and urban backgrounds. Advocacy groups have long argued that economic independence alone does not protect women when social structures normalize financial demands tied to marriage.

What Happens Next

Ankur remains in judicial custody. The investigation is ongoing, with police examining whether additional family members bear criminal liability for the alleged pattern of harassment. Kajal's one-and-a-half-year-old son is in the care of her parents.
nri_angle: The case highlights how dowry violence persists in India even among urban, government-employed families — a systemic issue the diaspora remains connected to through family networks and marriage practices.
author: Diaspora Desk
